You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 68-year-old man with advanced dementia is brought to the preoperative unit prior to an elective cholecystectomy for biliary colic. He says he does not want the surgery anymore. He begins yelling at unit staff and requests to leave. His designated medical power of attorney, who had previously signed the surgery consent forms, is present. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

Options:
A. Consult psychiatry for capacity evaluation
B. Cancel the surgery and allow the patient to leave
C. Ask the patient about his concerns and try to address them
D. Call family members and schedule a family meeting
E. Perform cognitive screening evaluation

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns decision‑making capacity and surrogate consent in a patient with dementia, which falls under psychiatric/mental health evaluation."}
